rows.basis: The FY2024 MD&A says Vertiv 'is increasing capacity to support additional demand for AI infrastructure' and the Q2 2024 release says it will keep investing in capacity, but neither gives an amount or share. The 167.0M total capex is factory capacity for all customers, not the AI part. The PP&E category increases are not tied to data-center demand.

The Q1 and Q2 2025 releases and the FY2025 MD&A describe capacity expansion 'particularly in AI infrastructure deployments' and for 'data centers and other mission-critical applications', with no amount. The 220.0M total capex is not the AI part. The large rise in machinery and equipment (570.1M to 874.1M gross) is not attributed by the company.

The FY2023 MD&A says Vertiv is increasing capacity for AI infrastructure demand, without a figure. The 175 to 200M FY2024 capex plan in the Q4 2023 release is a company total 'to support the growth trajectory', not an AI amount.
The FY2024 MD&A says Vertiv will 'continue to invest to support additional growth driven by AI'. It gives no amount or share.

The FY2025 MD&A says Vertiv is 'increasing capacity to support additional demand for AI infrastructure as necessary'. It gives no amount or share; Q2 2026 guidance of about 4% of revenue is total capex.
The FY2023 MD&A says Vertiv invested in new products, services and solutions for the AI trend. It gives no ER&D or opex amount attributed to AI.
The FY2024 MD&A repeats that Vertiv invested in products and solutions for the AI-driven industry. It gives no figure.

The Q1 and Q2 2025 releases cite 'significant ER&D investments in next-generation technologies and AI-optimized infrastructure solutions'. They give no amount, so no part of the 1,885.5M opex can be attributed.

The FY2022 MD&A attributes sales increases partly to 'deployment of large colocation data centers'; data center, not AI, and no figure. The regional segments (Americas 2,728.6M) are not data-center lines.

The Q3 2024 release says AI development 'is driving demand across our entire AI-enabling portfolio' and cites Vertiv's role in AI and data centers; no data-center or AI share is stated. The regional segments are not data-center lines and are not summed.

The Q2 2025 release ties net sales of 2,638M (a company total for the quarter, not data-center revenue) to 'robust data center demand'; data center, not AI, and no share stated. Americas segment revenue of 6,386.3M is a region, not a data-center line.

none_found.reason: No statement links FY2022 capex to AI or data-center demand. The company gives no PP&E category tied to AI.
No statement in the pack ties FY2023 capex to AI with words or a number.
No statement attributes FY2022 opex to AI, and there is no segment cost line.
No revenue statement for FY2023 in the pack, and the regional segments are not data-center lines.

Vertiv does not state a data-center or AI share of revenue in any year. Its segments are regional, and the thesis bars whole_business. The FY2021 and FY2026 statements fall outside the pack's value years.
